newsitem.title: JAPAN: North Korea to release U.S. detainee on Tuesday - U.S..
newsitem.headline: North Korea to release U.S. detainee on Tuesday - U.S..

text.p: The U.S. embassy in Tokyo said on Monday that North Korea will release American Carl Hunziker, who has been detained in the communist state for three months on espionage charges.
"Congressman Bill Richardson will return (to Tokyo) from North Korea on Tuesday with Mr Evan Carl Hunziker on a U.S. military aircraft...," the embassy said in a statement.
Richardson had earlier flown from Tokyo to the North Korean capital Pyongyang on Monday in the hope of bringing back Hunziker.
Hunziker, 26, was arrested on August 24 after crossing the Yalu River from China into North Korea and accused of being a U.S. spy. Hunziker's family has denied the charge, saying he is a missionary.
Richardson, a Democrat from New Mexico, was to act as an unofficial U.S. envoy in negotiations with North Korean officials.

U.S. State Department officials described Richardson's visit as "an important humanitarian mission", although he would be accompanied by a U.S. State Department official acting as an "escort officer".
Richardson has served as Washington's troubleshooter on several previous missions to countries which have no formal diplomatic ties with the United States, such as North Korea.
In December 1994, Richardson visited North Korea to negotiate the release of a U.S. pilot whose helicopter was brought down in North Korean airspace.
He had planned to visit North Korea in September but the trip was called off after an intrusion by a North Korean submarine into South Korean waters sparked a major crisis between the two Koreas.
The two Koreas technically remain at war since the 1950-53 Korean War ended without a peace agreement.

Japan's Kyodo news agency reported that Richardson would be aiming to secure Hunziker's immediate release in exchange for a sum of money. Hunziker's family have agreed to pay $5,000 for his release, the agency said.
Kyodo said North Korea had demanded $100,000 for Hunziker's release, but the United States had rejected the demand on the grounds that the amount was too high.
Officials from the U.S. embassy in Tokyo were unable to comment on the Kyodo report.
